rows.note: This is the all-purpose way to say that you send a text to someone.

example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 faat3 dyun2 seon3 bei2 nei5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for written text or wording in general.

example.english: I’ve read this text three times and still don’t understand it.
example.traditional: 呢段文字我睇咗三次都仲係唔明。
example.jyutping: ni1 dyun6 man4 zi6 ngo5 tai2 zo2 saam1 ci3 dou1 zung6 hai6 m4 ming4

rows.note: Use this for a particular passage, article, or piece of writing rather than text in the abstract.

example.english: Can you check this text for typos?
example.traditional: 你幫我睇吓呢篇文有冇錯字？
example.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 haa5 ni1 pin1 man4 jau5 mou5 co3 zi6

rows.note: Use this when the text is an article, composition, or other substantial written work.

example.english: This text is really well written; have a look when you have time.
example.traditional: 呢篇文章寫得好好，你得閒睇吓。
example.jyutping: nei1 pin1 man4 zoeng1 se2 dak1 hou2 hou2 nei5 dak1 haan4 tai2 haa5

rows.note: Use this only for a passage in a textbook or lesson.

example.english: We have to memorize this text for dictation next week.
example.traditional: 呢篇課文下星期要默書。
example.jyutping: ni1 pin1 fo3 man4 haa6 sing1 kei4 jiu3 mak6 syu1

rows.note: Use this when the focus is texting with someone back and forth rather than sending one message.

example.english: I text my mum every day to chat.
example.traditional: 我成日同阿媽發短訊傾偈。
example.jyutping: ngo5 seng4 jat6 tung4 aa3 maa1 faat3 dyun2 seon3 king1 gai2
